question: In December 2024, as per Ministry of New and Renewable Energy the number of installations under the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana are expected to reach ________ crores by March 2027.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) has launched several initiatives to promote solar energy usage in India, including the **PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana**.
 
• As per projections by MNRE, the number of installations under this scheme is expected to reach **1 crore** by **March 2027**. This estimation is based on the pace of implementation and adoption of solar energy technologies in households.
 
• The scheme aims to provide **free solar electricity** to households by encouraging the installation of solar panels on rooftops and other accessible areas.
 
• India has been actively working towards achieving its renewable energy targets, with a focus on increasing the contribution of **solar energy** to its electricity grid. The PM Surya Ghar Yojana is part of this effort to decentralize energy generation and reduce dependency on conventional sources.
 
• By March 2027, with the successful implementation of the scheme, it is expected to benefit millions of households by reducing electricity costs and contributing to a greener environment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana:**

 
 
• The scheme is primarily targeted at promoting **solar panel installations** in urban and rural households, thereby reducing electricity bills.
 
• It aims to make solar energy accessible and affordable for all citizens of India, particularly those in the **lower-income groups**.
 
• Under the initiative, households can install rooftop solar panels at **minimal or no cost** due to subsidies and financial support provided by the government.
 
• The scheme contributes to achieving India's renewable energy goals, including the target of **500 GW non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030** as pledged under the Paris Agreement.
 
 
 
• **India’s Renewable Energy Targets:**
 
 
• India has set ambitious targets under its **National Solar Mission**, aiming for 100 GW of solar energy capacity by 2022. Although this target is yet to be fully achieved, the government continues to push for advancements in solar technology.
 
• As of **October 2023**, India has achieved over **70 GW** of solar energy capacity, with ongoing efforts to enhance installations.
 
• Adoption of schemes like PM Surya Ghar contributes to decentralized energy generation and strengthens rural electrification efforts.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of Solar Energy:**
 
 
• Solar energy is a **clean and sustainable source** of power that helps reduce carbon emissions.
 
• It offers **cost savings** for households and businesses by reducing dependency on conventional electricity grids.
 
• India’s geographical location provides it with ample sunlight, making solar energy highly viable.
 
 
 
• **MNRE’s Role:**
 
 
• The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) is the nodal agency responsible for promoting renewable energy initiatives in India.
 
• It provides **financial support, policy guidelines**, and assistance to implement schemes like PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana.
 
• MNRE has introduced several other programs, such as **KUSUM Scheme** and **Solar Parks**, to enhance solar energy adoption across sectors.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Option 1 (5 crores):** Unrealistic given the current pace of installations and resource availability under the scheme.
 
• **Option 2 (1 crore):** Accurate according to official projections by MNRE for installations under PM Surya Ghar Yojana by March 2027.
 
• **Option 3 (2.5 crores):** Overestimation based on available data and implementation pace.
 
• **Option 4 (3 crores):** Unlikely due to resource constraints and adoption rates.
